cambridge-iccs/ftorch.manifest:
name="ftorch"
version="2.0.0"
license="MIT"
[library]
source-dir="playground-library"
include-dir=["src"]
[build]
auto-executables=false
auto-examples=false
auto-tests=false
link=["torch","torch_cpu","c10","stdc++"]
[install]
library=true
[preprocess.cpp]
macros=["GPU_DEVICE=0", "GPU_DEVICE_CUDA=1", "GPU_DEVICE_HIP=1", "GPU_DEVICE_MPS=13", "GPU_DEVICE_NONE=0", "GPU_DEVICE_XPU=12", "USE_C10D_GLOO", "USE_C10D_MPI", "USE_DISTRIBUTED", "USE_RPC", "USE_TENSORPIPE"]

scope: The original FTorch Fortran and C++ sources are wrapped for FPM, using pinned Debian CPU LibTorch 2.6.0+dfsg-7, the C++20 mode, C++11 ABI and include/definition settings from the upstream CMake target. The operator C++ flag setting is restricted to a current, unshared source-package recipe; public requests cannot set it and previous cache keys are preserved. The self-contained consumer embeds a reproducibly generated 1,766-byte TorchScript model as hexadecimal text, writes tiny.pt in the sandbox and calls the author tensor/model API in REAL64. Two different five-element inputs exercise y=2*x+1, with each output checked independently for finiteness and absolute error below 1e-12. The second call also verifies that the input tensor observes updated Fortran storage. No Python or model download runs in visitor jobs. This is an illustrative affine inference model, not a trained scientific predictor. K covers inference as function approximation; no training or optimization classification is inferred. GPU use, training, autograd, parallel execution and arbitrary external models are not verified. FTorch MIT notices and native Debian dependency notices are retained. APT estimates about 924 MB of additional native dependencies in the isolated FTorch image; these are separate from the catalog logical library-artifact total.

native_runtime.estimate_note: APT rounded decimal MB for the package-specific native dependencies; excludes compiler/library artifacts. This is not a billing measurement.
native_runtime.scope: FTorch image only; other packages do not inherit LibTorch.

initial_driver_correction: The first prototype main used a character PARAMETER substring as an internal READ unit, which gfortran rejects. Copying the hex pair into a character variable fixes the driver. All original FTorch library sources compiled; no upstream numerical or interface changes were made.
